messages.content:
What is asked:
<data>
Run-length encoding of a list of natural numbers. Every maximal run of equal neighbours becomes one pair: the value, and how long the run is. The pairs stand in the order of the runs.
</data>

The name and the signature:
<data>
def runLengths (l : List Nat) : List (Nat × Nat)
</data>

The last version:
<data>
/-- The maximal runs of equal neighbours in `l`, in order, each as its value and its length; the empty list has no runs. -/
def runLengths (l : List Nat) : List (Nat × Nat) :=
  match l with
  | [] => []
  | x :: rest =>
    match runLengths rest with
    | (y, n) :: tail => if x = y then (y, n + 1) :: tail else (x, 1) :: tail
    | [] => [(x, 1)]
</data>

What happened to it:
<data>
The definition compiles. It gets these examples wrong:
- runLengths [1, 1, 2, 3, 3, 3]  should give  [(1, 2), (2, 1), (3, 3)]  and gives  [(1, 2)]
- (runLengths [5, 5, 6, 5]).length  should give  3  and gives  1
</data>

Versions that were tried before, and are not to be repeated:
<data>
/-- The maximal runs of equal neighbours in `l`, in order, each as its value and its length; the empty list has no runs. -/
def runLengths (l : List Nat) : List (Nat × Nat) :=
  match l with
  | [] => []
  | x :: rest =>
    let run := rest.takeWhile (· == x)
    (x, run.length + 1) :: runLengths (rest.dropWhile (· == x))
</data>
